question: Why does a pair that completes within its capture timeout still compare almost none of its discovered glyphs, leaving most of the document as material no comparison examined?

stage_attribution.method: temporary stderr counters at each candidate producer, reverted after measurement

append_text_candidates.append_nonexact_g.note: A non-exhaustive group search discards every proposal it found, so this stage contributes nothing.

experiments.result: examined_pairs 1170 -> 10136, proposals found 992 -> 10000, still not exhaustive because max_proposals is 10000, still all discarded. No coverage change.
experiments.conclusion: The work budget is not the binding constraint.

experiments.change: keep the partial proposal set instead of truncating it
experiments.result: exit 2, 'correspondence descendant ownership exceeded its limit of 1000000'
experiments.conclusion: The truncation is load-bearing: it is what keeps this pair from failing the way jvms-se17-to-se21 and libreoffice-getting-started-74-to-75 fail. Those exit-2 pairs and the low-coverage pairs are the same condition seen from two sides.

experiments.change: keep the partial set AND raise max_ownership_visits 1e6 -> 64e6
experiments.result: exit 3. old_compared_sources 193, new 190, accepted_correspondences 4 — identical to baseline. Only scope unresolved fell from 21 to 16.
experiments.conclusion: 10,000 additional proposals produced zero additional accepted correspondences. Neither budget nor truncation is the limiting factor; the correspondence solver accepts almost nothing on this document.

findings: PipelineOptions::scaled_limits scales only native-pipeline limits (n-gram elements, alignment visits, DP cells, diff tokens, edit distance, assessment work and ranges). It does not touch MatchingLimits, so --limit-scale has no effect on the shared-evidence route at all. Every corpus pair runs the document matcher at fixed defaults regardless of its registered limit_scale_hint.

The non-exact group search cannot be exhaustive at this document size: 714 x 417 candidate endpoints against a 10,000-proposal ceiling. Its output is therefore always discarded on documents of this scale.
Raising the work and ownership budgets 64x leaves accepted correspondences unchanged at 4. The blocker is correspondence acceptance, not enumeration or budget.

That is where the 0.14% comes from, and no limit exposed on the command line moves it.
